overview.problemStatement: Attendees need to find relevant events and register without friction, while every registration must produce a ticket that can be verified at the door.
overview.proposedSolution: Public explore surfaces (featured, nearby, popular, category and location routes, title search), a slug-based public event page, a Clerk-authenticated registration flow that issues a QR ticket, and a My Tickets page where attendees view or cancel registrations.
overview.targetAudience: Event attendees in Nigeria, including signed-out visitors who browse and signed-in attendees who register and manage tickets.
assumptions: retroactive: true - documented from the existing implementation during brownfield onboarding; it is not a forward-looking product decision.
Paid tickets are settled offline at the venue; no payment processor is integrated.
The default country is Nigeria and prices are displayed in naira.
Currency, tax, and refund policy are not modelled.
outOfScope: Waitlists when an event is full.

userStories.title: Browse featured, nearby, and popular events
userStories.want: one explore page that shows featured, nearby, popular events, and category counts
userStories.benefit: I can find something worth attending without knowing what to search for

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given upcoming events exist, when I open /explore, then I see a featured carousel (up to 4), events near my saved city/state (default Port Harcourt, Rivers), popular events (up to 6), and a category grid with counts.
Given data is loading or empty, when I open /explore, then each section shows its own loading or empty state and the page still renders the remaining sections.

userStories.title: Browse by category or location
userStories.want: a category or city page with pagination
userStories.benefit: I can narrow the catalogue to what interests me

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given I select a category or view all nearby events, when /explore/[slug] loads, then the slug resolves as a category id or a city-state location slug and shows up to 10 upcoming events with pagination.
Given a slug matches neither a category nor a valid location, then the route renders not-found instead of an empty list.

userStories.title: Inspect an event before registering
userStories.want: a public event page with full details and the correct call to action
userStories.benefit: I can decide whether to attend

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a valid event slug, when I open /events/[slug], then I see title, description, date/time, location, organizer, price, and registration count vs capacity; an unknown slug renders not-found.
Given the event state, the sidebar CTA is View Ticket when registered, disabled Event Ended when past, disabled Event Full when full, Manage Event for the organizer, and Register otherwise.

userStories.title: Register and receive a QR ticket
userStories.want: to register with my name and email and receive a QR ticket
userStories.benefit: I can prove my registration at the door

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given I am signed out, when I press Register for Event, then I am told to sign in and no registration is created.
Given I am signed in and submit a non-empty name and email, then a confirmed registration is stored with a unique EVT-... QR code and the event registration count increases by one.
Given the event is full registration is rejected, given I am already confirmed a duplicate is rejected, and given my earlier registration was cancelled it is reactivated and the count increments.

userStories.title: Manage my tickets
userStories.want: to see upcoming and past tickets and cancel one

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given I have registrations, when I open /my-tickets, then upcoming confirmed and past/cancelled tickets are listed separately and selecting a ticket shows its QR code and ticket ID.
Given I own a confirmed registration, when I cancel it, then its status becomes cancelled and the event count decreases; another user's registration cannot be cancelled.

userStories.title: Personalise my event feed
userStories.want: to choose my city and interests
userStories.benefit: the surfaces I use show relevant events

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given I visit an attendee page for the first time, onboarding asks for at least three interests and a Nigerian state and city, and completion persists hasCompletedOnboarding, location, and interests.

userStories.title: Search events by title
userStories.want: to type a title and see matching upcoming events
userStories.benefit: I can jump straight to an event

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a query of at least two characters, search returns at most five upcoming events whose titles match; shorter or blank queries return an empty list.

functionalRequirements.text: The explore page MUST aggregate featured events, events near the attendee's saved location, popular events, and per-category counts.
The explore routes MUST resolve category ids and location slugs and MUST paginate results at ten per page.
The public event page MUST resolve an event by slug and expose its full details.
The public event page MUST select its call to action from registration, past, capacity, organizer, and default states.
Registration MUST require an authenticated Clerk user.
Registration MUST store the attendee name and email, issue a unique QR code, and increment the event registration count.
Registration MUST reject full events and confirmed duplicates, and MUST reactivate a cancelled registration.
My Tickets MUST list upcoming and past/cancelled registrations and display each QR ticket.
An attendee MUST be able to cancel only their own confirmed registration.
Attendee onboarding MUST capture at least three interests plus a state and city and persist them.
Event search MUST match titles for queries of at least two characters and return only upcoming events.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Discovery and ticket surfaces MUST remain usable at a 360px viewport and MUST expose loading and empty states.
Ownership and role checks MUST be enforced in Convex functions, not only in the client.
Registration input MUST be validated for a required name and email before the mutation runs.
The feature MUST pass ESLint, TypeScript checking, and SpecDrive governance validation before it is considered complete.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Registration is rejected with a full-event message and the CTA is disabled.

edgeCases.description: The user already has a confirmed registration.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: A duplicate is rejected and the page shows View Ticket.

edgeCases.description: The user previously cancelled their registration.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Registering reactivates the existing row and increments the count once.
The registration CTA is disabled and Event Ended is shown.
A sign-in message is shown and no mutation runs.
Each section shows an empty state and the page offers a create-event action.

dependencies.notes: App Router pages and client navigation.

dependencies.name: country-state-city
dependencies.notes: Nigerian states and cities for onboarding.

risks.mitigation: The registration mutation re-reads the event and re-checks capacity inside the transaction.

risks.description: QR codes are visible ticket identifiers and could be guessed.
risks.mitigation: Check-in is rate-limited per organizer and codes include a random UUID segment.

risks.description: Title-only search misses events whose names do not contain the query.
risks.mitigation: Category and location routes remain the primary discovery path.
